questions.q: What is the difference between variables.tf and a .tfvars file?
options: variables.tf is only used by modules, never by root configurations
.tfvars files declare types, while variables.tf supplies values
variables.tf declares what inputs exist and their types; a .tfvars file supplies the actual values to use
They do the exact same thing and can be used interchangeably
questions.explain: variables.tf declares what a configuration accepts and its types; dev.tfvars or prod.tfvars then supplies the concrete values for a specific environment.

questions.q: How do you tell terraform apply to use prod.tfvars instead of dev.tfvars?
options: Rename variables.tf to prod.tfvars
terraform workspace select prod.tfvars
terraform apply -var-file="prod.tfvars"
Terraform always loads every .tfvars file in the directory automatically
questions.explain: The -var-file flag explicitly names which .tfvars file to load for that plan/apply run.

questions.q: Which filenames does Terraform auto-load without needing -var-file?
options: Any file with a .tf extension
dev.tfvars and prod.tfvars, automatically, based on the active workspace
terraform.tfvars, and any file ending in .auto.tfvars
None — -var-file is always required for every .tfvars file
questions.explain: Terraform auto-loads a file literally named terraform.tfvars and any *.auto.tfvars file; other names require an explicit -var-file flag.

questions.q: In the lesson's worked example, what changes between applying with dev.tfvars versus prod.tfvars?
options: The provider block is replaced with a different cloud provider
A new workspace is automatically created
Only the input values (instance_count, vm_size) — the webapp module's code and main.tf stay identical
The module's source code is swapped for a different module
questions.explain: The same module, called from the same main.tf, receives different variable values depending on which .tfvars file was loaded — the logic itself never changes.

questions.q: How do .tfvars files relate to the workspaces and separate state files covered in Lessons 17–18?
options: They are a replacement for workspaces and make separate state files unnecessary
They control which backend a configuration uses
They can only be used together with workspaces, never with separate directories
They solve a different problem — what values an apply uses — and combine naturally with either approach to where state lives
questions.explain: Workspaces/separate state files control where state lives; .tfvars files control what values go into a given apply — a real project typically combines both ideas.
